subject: Re: Kickoff: advice-based moment estimation — May status + advice-staleness risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: baselines reproduced on the public graph datasets. On a skewed temporal graph, advice-based sampling cuts second-moment estimation error to roughly a third of PPSWOR at the same sample budget, and perfect advice shows another ~2x of headroom beyond that — so the learned-advice quality is what everything hinges on.

Which brings the risk: staleness. Freya trained advice on week N of telemetry and evaluated on week N+1 vs N+4. At N+1 we keep ~85% of the error reduction; at N+4 we keep barely half, and on one traffic shift (a datacenter drain that reshuffled the heavy IP pairs) stale advice was briefly worse than plain ell_1 sampling. Advice-guided sampling concentrates the budget where the advice says mass is — when the world moves, it concentrates in the wrong place.

Plan: weekly advice refresh as the recommended operating mode, plus a fallback that blends in ell_1 sampling when observed frequencies diverge from advice. The June full-scale run will quantify the blend.

Umar
